maria: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector change merged yesterday I'm seeing a p99 spike on short requests (<=64 tokens) when running the steadyflow scheduler. Dumped a trace; looks like a kernel handoff path that waits for coalescing then falls back to a cold kernel, adding ~60-90ms.
leo: Can you paste the perf trace + current scheduler config? which knobs were in play? :eyes:
maria: Repro command I used: `make perf-run MODEL=redwood-small SEQ=64 BURST=1`
Logs (snipped):
```
[trace] queue_wait=23ms coalesce_wait=40ms kernel_fallback=cold_init(72ms) total=135ms
[meta] max_batch_tokens=4096 max_wait_ms=12 kernel_selector=handoff-v3
[kv] hit_rate=0.61 primed=false
```
ryan: Hmm — handoff-v3 tries to prefer fused kernels which have larger init cost but better throughput. For short sequences that can backfire if KV hit-rate drops. What's p50/p95/p99 baseline vs after rollout?
maria: Baseline (pre-rollout) p50/p95/p99 = 6/24/82ms. After rollout: 5/30/145ms. Notable the KV hit_rate fell 0.87 -> 0.61 around the same time.
olga: That KV drop is suspicious — were we skipping priming on the new variant? If the priming path didn't run, a lot of short requests hit cold kernel init. Try priming short-prefix KV entries or a warmup pass at deploy. Also consider tuning batching thresholds instead of immediate fallback.
leo: Two quick experiments I'd run: (A) conservative kernel fallback: add a grace period (kernel_fallback_grace_ms=50) so we avoid switching to cold init inside short waits, (B) reduce max_batch_tokens to 2048 and raise max_wait_ms to 20ms so steadyflow coalesces smaller groups without invoking heavyweight kernels.
ryan: Agreed. Also add a per-model cold-kernel timeout that prefers the old fast kernel for <64 tokens until the fused kernel KV is warmed. That keeps p99 low while we harvest throughput for large sequences.
ci-bot: deploy/redwood-runtime v2.14 rolled at 3250000000 by @deploy-bot
maria: Kicking off both experiment variants now: (1) fallback_grace=50ms, (2) max_batch_tokens=2048,max_wait_ms=20. I'll run 30m perf sweep and post numbers.
leo: Nice. Also capture the KV prime hit-rate histogram alongside latency (1m buckets). If p99 tracks kv-hit_rate dips that confirms root cause.
maria: Ack — running. Posting results in ~25m. :thumbsup:
